title: Alex Warren Earns Second Consecutive U.K. No. 1 Album With ‘Wildchild’
summary: "You guys were the first ones to ever believe in me," the 25-year-old said of his U.K. audience.
contentText:
Alex Warren has clinched a second consecutive No. 1 album in the U.K. with his new set, Wildchild, debuting at the top of the U.K.’s Official Albums Chart published Friday (Sept. 4).

The achievement follows You’ll Be Alright, Kid , which reached the summit in July 2025 and spawned the Californian singer’s global smash hit “Ordinary”; the hit lasted 13 weeks atop the U.K.’s Official Singles Chart . He supported the release with a U.K. arena tour in April, which included two nights at London’s 20,000-capacity O2 Arena.

Reacting to the achievement, Warren told the Official Charts Company : “This is absolutely insane, and I just want to say thank you from the bottom of my heart. You guys were the first ones to ever believe in me, and I hope I can get over there [to the U.K.] pretty soon and do some shows. I love you so, so much!”

Manchester indie unit The Courteeners secure the runner-up spot with greatest hits compilation God Bless the Band . Michael Jackson ’s The Essential follows at No. 3, while Olivia Rodrigo ’s you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love remains at No. 4. Dolly Parton’s Diamonds & Rhinestones: The Greatest Hits Collection rounds out the top five following the country music icon’s death on Aug. 25.

Bananarama’s True Confessions vaults to a new peak of No. 6 following the release of its 40th anniversary edition. The result earns the British pop group its highest charting U.K. album in 38 years, following 1988’s The Greatest Hits Collection .

The Warning appears on the Official Albums Chart for the first time at No. 16 with Everything’s Falling , while further down the chart, Steve Hackett and Steve Rothery’s new collaborative effort, The Roaring Waves , finishes at No. 24.

Mastodon secures its sixth U.K. top 40 album with Marrow Deep at No. 27, while former Beastie Boy Mike D lands his first solo entry as Thank You debuts at No. 28. New York indie heroes Interpol’s newly released record, This Mirror Weighs a Ton , enters at No. 33.
